###### KNX Standard Resources Management

 4.3.22 PID_IO_LIST (PID = 71)

  - Property name: Interface Object List

  - Property Datatype: PDT_UNSIGNED_INT[]

  - Datapoint Type: DPT_Value_2_Ucount (7.001)

###### 4.3.22.1 Resource definition
This Property is mandatory if the Extended Data Property Services and/or the Extended Function
Property Services are implemented.

_PID_IO_LIST shall be a read-only, array structured Property with as much elements as Interface Objects_
are located (or “active”) in the device. The array element with index 0 shall contain the number of array
elements (this is, Interface Objects) implemented in the device. The Property shall contain the Interface
Object Types in ascending order of the object indexes, starting with the array field with index 1. For
Interface Objects with more than 1 instance, the 1[st] instance shall be at the position with the lower/lowest
index, the Interface Object Type of the 2[nd] instance shall be placed at the next index and so on.

###### 4.3.22.2 Usage by the Management Client

4.3.22.2.1 Remote access
The Management Client shall access this Property through

   - DMP_InterfaceOject_Read_RCl, or

   - DMP_InterfaceOject_Read_RCo if the Management Server supports connection-oriented
communication mode and a Transport Layer connection to the Management Server exists.

/* Read PID_IO_LIST of the Device Object */
DMP_InterfaceOject_Read_RCl( /* [IN] */ object_index = 0; /* [IN] */ PID = PID_IO_LIST,

/* [OUT] */ PID_IO_LIST = data)

###### 4.3.25 PID_RECEIVE_BLOCK_TABLE (PID = 75)

  - Property name: BiBat Receive Block Table

  - Property Datatype: PDT_UNSIGNED_CHAR[16]

  - Datapoint Type: None.

The Property BiBat Receive Block Table shall contain the activated receive blocks in the BiBat Slave,
which are assigned by the BiBat Master. The BiBat Slave shall activate its receiver in the corresponding
receive blocks.

The BiBat Master shall assign receive blocks to each BiBat Slave via a 128 bit table at configuration time
and may alter this receive block bit table as long as the average number of receive blocks signalled by the
BiBat Slave is not exceeded. The BiBat Master shall assign each such additional receive block to a single
BiBat Slave, a group of BiBat Slaves or to all BiBat Slaves.

Any BiBat Slave shall be able to receive sync or data frames in the first time slot of block #0 and block
#64 of each section, independent of the value of the Property BiBat Receive Block Table.

In the standard system the data length of a Property element is restricted to 10 octets. Therefore the table
shall be encoded as an array Property with 16 elements (16 x 1 octet). The BiBat Master shall use two or
more messages to write the complete Property BiBat Receive Block Table. Because of the segmented
write access to the table, the BiBat Slave cannot check, whether the table data is consistent. The BiBat
Master shall ensure complete download of the table.

© Copyright 1999 - 2021, KNX Association System Specifications v01.10.01 - page 76 of 77

|• <br>not allowed|1|0|

Each of the 128 bits of the table shall represent a block. The mapping of the block# to the corresponding
bit in the table is shown above.

If the bit is set to ’1’, the corresponding receive-block shall be active.

If the bit is set to ’0’, the corresponding receive-block shall be inactive.

The table fields for block #0 and blocks #64 shall always contain the value ‘1’.

The table shall be stored by the BiBat Slave in non-volatile memory.

###### 4.3.26 PID_RANDOM_PAUSE_TABLE (PID = 76)

  - Property name: BiBat Random Pause Table

  - Property Datatype: PDT_UNSIGNED_CHAR[12]

  - Datapoint Type: None.

Every BiBat Master shall maintain a unique table of 12 values for the length of 12 subsequent random
pauses. It shall distribute this random pause table to all its BiBat Slaves during configuration. The table
shall be derived from the unique 48 bit KNX Serial Number of the BiBat Master.

Each table element shall be encoded on 8 bit (transport format).
- The allowed range of each value is 0 to 15 (lower 4 bit) corresponding to a random pause length of
0 s to 0,937 5 s.
- The upper 4 bit of each table element are fixed 0000b.

In the BiBat Slave the table may be stored in a packed format (e.g. two 4 bit table values in one octet).

###### KNX Standard Resources Management

In the standard system the data length of a Property element is restricted to 10 octets. Therefore the table
shall be encoded as an array Property with 12 elements (12 x 1 octet). The BiBat Master shall use two or
more messages to write the complete Property BiBat Random Pause Table. Because of the segmented
write access to the table, the BiBat Slave cannot check, whether the table data is consistent. The BiBat
Master shall ensure complete download of the table.

The BiBat Slave shall store the table in non-volatile memory

To allow the BiBat Slave to resynchronise fully to the BiBat Master, the ‘Help Call Response’ message
shall contain a random pause pointer value (0 to 11).

- Random pause pointer value 0 to 11: points to the corresponding element 1 to 12 of the random
pause table (n+1)

- 13[th] random pause, fixed length 1 s (value 10h)

###### 4.3.27 PID_RECEIVE_BLOCK_NR (PID = 77)

  - Property name: BiBat Receive Block Number

  - Property Datatype: PDT_UNSIGNED_CHAR

  - Datapoint Type: None.

A synchronous BiBat Slave may signal a higher receive frequency (= smaller reception period) to the
BiBat Master at configuration time. The Property BiBat Receive Block Number shall contain the
(average) number of additional receive blocks (0 to 126) within a 128 block section in addition to the
minimum (default). The BiBat Master shall check the number of additional receive blocks during
configuration and shall then assign receive blocks to each BiBat Slave via the 128 bit Property BiBat
Receive Block Number. The BiBat Master may alter this Property BiBat Receive Block Number as long
as the average number of receive blocks signalled by the BiBat Slave is not exceeded.

The Property is mandatory and shall be read-only.

Value 0 is allowed and shall mean “no additional receive-blocks”.

###### 4.3.29 PID_RETRANSMITTER_NUMBER (PID = 79)

  - Property name: BiBat Retransmitter Number

  - Property Datatype: PDT_UNSIGNED_CHAR

  - Datapoint Type: None.

The Property BiBat Retransmitter Number shall be assigned by the BiBat Master during configuration
and shall define time delay of the Retransmitter.

Range: values 1 to 3 are allowed values that shall be assigned by the BiBat Master.

The default value in the Retransmitter at manufacturing time shall be 0. The value 0 shall indicate that the
Retransmitter is unconfigured, this is, it is not active for synchronous communication

The Retransmitter shall store the value of the Property BiBat Retransmitter Number in non-volatile
memory.

###### 4.3.30 PID_SERIAL_NR_TABLE (PID = 80)

  - Property name: KNX Serial Number Table

  - Property Datatype: PDT_GENERIC_06[]

  - Datapoint Type: DPT_SerNum (221.001)

###### 4.3.30.1 Use
The KNX Serial Number Table Property shall contain the KNX Serial Numbers of the associated
RF transmit-only devices.

Implementation of the KNX Serial Number Table is mandatory in RF bidirectional devices if the product
has the ability to interwork with transmit-only devices.

Reading out of the KNX Serial Number Table by a Management Client, tool, like ETS, shall be possible.
Setting of the KNX Serial Number Table by a Management Client, like ETS, is optional.

 4.3.30.2 Format
The KNX Serial Number Table Property shall be an array of 6 octet KNX Serial Numbers. The table shall
contain the KNX Serial Numbers of linked devices or void table elements as specified below.

**Array Index** **Value**

1 1[st] KNX Serial Number (6 Octets)

2 2[nd] KNX Serial Number (6 Octets)

3 ….

… …

N …

**Figure 9 – Structure of the KNX Serial Number Table**

###### 4.3.30.3 Usage by the Management Server (device)

4.3.30.3.1 Usage by LTE RF BD devices
The KNX Serial Number Table shall be generated by the device itself during linking with
RF transmit-only devices.

− For each additional RF transmit-only partner device that is linked to this Management Server
(device) the corresponding KNX Serial Number shall be added in the list (last element + 1). The
table elements need not to be sorted.

− The maximal size of the table shall be fixed and product specific and the number of devices that can
be associated is therefore limited.

− Ex-factory, the table shall be empty and void table elements shall contain the KNX Serial Number
000000000000h.

− There may be gaps in the table with void table elements.

− Handling of full table

In case of insufficient table size the handling can be manufacturer specific; it is recommended to
generate an error indication and not to overwrite existing table elements.

− Deletion of individual table elements

The deletion of individual links is not foreseen in this standard but it shall be possible to reset
the whole table by manufacturer specific means.

− Write access to the table shall be optional (e.g. by ETS)

− Individual table elements can be written. There is no table load state machine.

− The current length N of the table Property shall be readable by means of an
A_PropertyDescription_Read-service.

4.3.30.3.2 Usage by BiBat Retransmitter
The Property in the BiBat Retransmitter shall at least contain the KNX Serial Number of the BiBat
Master of which the BiBat Retransmitter shall retransmit the synchronous and asynchronous telegrams.

The KNX Serial Number of the BiBat Master shall be assigned to element 1 of the table.

NOTE 13 BiBat Retransmitters shall retransmit synchronous telegrams only with the Domain Address of the BiBat System or the
KNX Serial Number of the BiBat Master. Selective retransmission/filtering (according to KNX Serial Numbers) of asynchronous
telegrams from other devices is an optional feature of the BiBat Retransmitter.

In addition to the BiBat Master KNX Serial Number, the table may contain the KNX Serial Numbers of
other devices for selective retransmission of asynchronous telegrams.

© Copyright 1999 - 2021, KNX Association System Specifications v01.10.01 - page 80 of 81

|Array Index|Value|
|---|---|
|1|1st KNX Serial Number (6 Octets)|
|2|2nd KNX Serial Number (6 Octets)|
|3|….|
|…|…|
|N|…|

###### KNX Standard Resources Management

**Rule for selective retransmission and filtering**

**a)** If the Property KNX Serial Number Table contains only one element (i.e. the KNX Serial
Number of the BiBat Master) then

      - asynchronous telegrams containing any KNX Serial Number shall systematically be
retransmitted; and
      - asynchronous telegrams containing the Domain Address of the BiBat System shall be
retransmitted; and
      - synchronous telegrams with the corresponding KNX Serial Number of the BiBat Master
shall be retransmitted, all other synchronous telegrams shall be discarded.

**b)** If the Property KNX Serial Number table contains more than one element then

      - asynchronous telegrams containing the KNX Serial Number of the sender shall be filtered
according to the Property KNX Serial Number Table; and
      - asynchronous telegrams containing the Domain Address of the BiBat System shall be
retransmitted; and
      - synchronous telegrams with the KNX Serial Number of the BiBat Master shall be
retransmitted, all other synchronous telegrams shall be discarded.

The Property KNX Serial Number table shall be set by the BiBat Master at configuration-time and shall
be stored in non-volatile memory.

The Property KNX Serial Number Table shall be an array of 6 octet KNX Serial Numbers. The table shall
contain KNX Serial Numbers used by the retransmitter for filtering or void table elements as specified
below.
- The size of the table shall be fixed and product specific and the number of devices that can be
associated shall therefore be limited.
- The length of the table Property shall be readable by means of A_PropertyDescription_Read.
- The BiBat Master shall check the maximum size of the table using A_PropertyDescription_Read
before writing the table.
- The table shall have no load state machine. Therefore all elements shall be written by the BiBat
Master.
- The table elements need not to be sorted. Element 1 shall however contain the KNX Serial Number
of the BiBat Master.
- Ex-factory, the table shall be empty and void table elements shall contain the KNX Serial Number
000000000000h.
- There may be “gaps” in the table with void table elements.
   - Erasing individual table elements is possible by writing the KNX Serial Number 000000000000h
to the corresponding element.

   - Write access to the table is mandatory in the BiBat retransmitter.

**Array Index** **Value**

1 1[st] KNX Serial Number (6 octets): of the BiBat Master

2 2[nd] KNX Serial Number (6 octets): of any other device

3 3[rd] KNX Serial Number (6 octets): of any other device

… …

N …

**Figure 10 – Encoding of the KNX Serial Number Table**

|Array Index|Value|
|---|---|
|1|1st KNX Serial Number (6 octets): of the BiBat Master|
|2|2nd KNX Serial Number (6 octets): of any other device|
|3|3rd KNX Serial Number (6 octets): of any other device|
|…|…|
|N|…|

 4.3.31 PID_BIBAT_MASTER_ADDRESS (PID = 81)

  - Property name: BiBat Master Individual Address

  - Property Datatype: PDT_UNSIGNED_INT

  - Datapoint Type: None.

The Property BiBat Master Individual Address shall contain the Individual Address of the BiBat Master.
The BiBat Slave needs the BiBat Master’s Individual Address as Destination Address in the help call.

This Property shall be set by the BiBat Master at configuration-time.

The BiBat Slave shall store the value in non-volatile memory.

###### 4.3.32 PID_RF_DOMAIN_ADDRESS (PID = 82)

  - Property name: RF Domain Address

  - Property Datatype: PDT_GENERIC_06

  - Datapoint Type: None.

4.3.32.1.1 PID_RF_DOMAIN_ADDRESS in the Device Object of the cEMI Server
The Property PID_RF_DOMAIN_ADDRESS shall contain the value of the Domain Address of the cEMI
Server that shall be used for filtering or that shall be inserted in the transmitted RF frame if the
L_Data.req contains the Domain Address 000000000000h; see [12] clause 4.1.4.3.2 “RF medium
information”.

NOTE 14 This is a different Property than PID_DOMAIN_ADDRESS (PID = 70) that is used on the Powerline communication
medium and that has a size of only two octets.

PID_RF_DOMAIN_ADDRESS shall be stored in non-volatile memory.

###### 4.3.33 PID_DEVICE_DESCRIPTOR (PID = 83)

  - Property name: Device Descriptor

  - Property Datatype: PDT_GENERIC_02

  - Datapoint Type: None.

This Property shall contain the Device Descriptor Type 0 of the device.

The format and coding shall be identical to what is specified in clause 4.1.2.

The value of this Property shall be identical to the value of the device’s Device Descriptor Type 0 value
as accessed though any other method, such as (not exclusive)

   - the Device Descriptor Type 0 value provided using the dedicated Application Layer service
A_DeviceDescriptor_Read. For use please refer to [09], e.g. Management Procedures
NM_IndividualAddress_Write, NM_IndividualAddress_SerialNumber_Write2,
NM_DomainAndIndividualAddress_Write, NM_DomainAndIndividualAddress_Write2,
NM_IndividualAddress_Check, DMP_Connect_RCo, DMP_Connect_RCl, etc.

###### 4.3.34 PID_GROUP_TELEGR_RATE_LIMIT_TIME_BASE (PID = 85)

  - Property name: group telegram rate limitation time base

  - Property Datatype: PDT_UNSIGNED_INT

  - Datapoint Type: None.

The “group telegram rate limitation time base” shall be a 2 octet unsigned value. Its unit shall be 1 ms. So
time bases from 1 ms to 65 535 ms can be encoded.

EXAMPLE A time base value of 10 000 shall indicate a time base of 10 s.

###### KNX Standard Resources Management

 4.3.34.1 Usage by the Management Server (device)
Within “group telegram rate limitation time base” the device shall at maximum transmit a number of
frames equal to the “group telegram rate limitation number of telegrams”. If the “group telegram rate
limitation number of telegrams” is set to 1 the time base shall indicate the minimum interframe time
between any two group telegrams.

If the time base value is set to zero then the telegram rate limitation shall be disabled independently of the
value of “group telegram rate limitation number of telegrams”.

**Table 21 - Group telegram rate limitation time base values**

**Value** **Meaning**

0 Group telegram rate limitation shall be disabled. The system shall not limit the number of
telegrams that may be transmitted within any period.

1 to 65 535 Time Base Value multiplied with 1 ms

PID_GROUP_TELEGR_RATE_LIMIT_TIME_BASE shall always be implemented together with
PID_GROUP_TELEGR_RATE_LIMIT_NO_OF_TELEGR. For further specifications and requirements,
please refer to clause 4.3.35.

###### 4.3.34.2 Usage by the Management Client
Please refer to clause 4.3.35.

###### 4.3.35 PID_GROUP_TELEGR_RATE_LIMIT_NO_OF_TELEGR (PID = 86)

  - Property name: group telegram rate limitation number of telegrams

  - Property Datatype: PDT_UNSIGNED_INT

  - Datapoint Type: None.

###### 4.3.35.1 Usage by the Management Server (device)
The “telegram rate limitation number of telegrams” shall be a 2 octet unsigned value for the number of
telegrams that shall be sent at maximum by a device within “telegram rate limitation time base”.

Valid data for “telegram rate limitation number of telegrams” are 0 to 65 535.

If the number of telegrams value is set to zero telegram rate limitation shall be disabled independently
from the “telegram rate limitation time base” value.

**Table 22 - Group telegram rate limitation number of telegrams values**

**Value** **Meaning**
0 Telegram rate limitation is disabled. The system shall not limit the number of telegrams
that may be transmitted within any period

1 to 65 535 Number of group telegrams to be transmitted at maximum within “telegram rate
limitation time base”.

Group telegram rate limitation functionality via Properties is an optional feature for devices. But if
implemented both Properties “group telegram rate limitation time base” and “group telegram rate
limitation number of telegrams” shall be implemented.

Both Properties shall be readable and at least one of them shall be writeable.
If “group telegram rate limitation number of telegrams” is set to 1 the interframe time mechanism shall be
active. If “group telegram rate limitation number of telegrams” is greater than 1 the number of group
telegrams within the time base shall be counted and limited.

###### KNX Standard Resources Management

 4.3.35.2 Usage by the Management Client
**Normal conditions**

The Properties “group telegram rate limitation time base” and “group telegram rate limitation number of
telegrams” shall be accessed through the Property mechanisms DMP_InterfaceObjectWrite_R,
DMP_InterfaceObjectVerify_R and DMP_InterfaceObjectRead_R.

Management telegrams are not limited by the group telegram rate limitation functionality.

**Error and exception handling**

If the Management Server does not support the group telegram rate limitation Properties, Property
description read access will fail.

In case the write access to the Properties “group telegram rate limitation time base” or “group telegram
rate limitation number of telegrams” fails, then the Management Client shall skip these accesses and
proceed with the rest of the download procedure.

These Properties of the Device Object shall provide the parameter blocks for Channel 1 to 32 of the
E-Mode Device. The value shall be an array of octets. Its content is defined in the specification of the
Channel by the Application Groups. The actual length is static, and depends on the corresponding
Channel Code.

**Error handling**

A negative response (no data) shall be sent each time one of following events appears in the request:

###### KNX Standard Resources Management

##### 4.4 Applicationprogram Object (Object Type 3)

###### 4.4.1 PID_OPERATION_MODE (PID: 52)

**●** **Property name:** **Operation Mode**

**●** **Property Datatype:** PDT_FUNCTION (alt.: PDT_VARIABLE_LENGTH)

**●** **Datapoint Type:** None.

**●** **Access policy:** 15F/00C

**●** **Access level:** 3/3

###### 4.4.1.1 Abstract Resource Definition
The Operation Mode shall serve to set and read the behaviour of the application program. This shall
mainly serve diagnostic purposes. The default Operation Mode shall be “Normal Mode”.

The Operation Mode shall only have effect if the Load State is “Loaded” and the run state is “Running”.
The Operation Mode shall not be an alternative to the Run State.

**Definition of the Operation Modes**

1. Normal Mode

a. The application shall be running unchanged; the application shall have access to the Group
Object value and the Group Object runtime flags.

b. The AL-service primitives shall be handled by the Group Object server, this is, the GO can be
read - and written by the A_GroupValue_Read and –Write-services.

c. Some Group Object Diagnostic commands shall not be accepted, as listed in Table 34.

2. Diagnostic Mode

This shall allow the MaC to make the application is explicitly aware of its influence.

a. The application may be running unchanged or may be halted; but the application shall have no
access to the Group Object value or the Group Object runtime flags.

NOTE 17 This shall prevent that a GO-value that is set by the MaC is immediately changed by a
(coincidental) subsequent access by the application, or that a request by the MaC to send a certain GOvalue is immediately overwritten by a coincidental spontaneous immediate next transmission by the
application. It shall also prevent that the application reads a received updated value of a GO before the
MaC has had the time and possibility to read the GO runtime flags.
b. The Group Objects shall not be updated by the communication stack by any sender other than
the one(s) possibly filtered by the MaC.

NOTE 18 This shall prevent that, if the MaC forces a device 1 to send a value on a GA 1, received
by a device 2, that this value is overwritten by a coincidental next spontaneous transmission by a device 3;
if this would not be the case, then the MaC has no possibility to conclude whether the communication
between device 1 and device 2 would be working properly or not.
**Constraints**

- Only one single Operation Mode is foreseen. There exist KNX devices with a second Application
Program (Application Program 2), which is however controlled (started and stopped) by the first
Application Program and which shall follow the Operation Mode of the Application Program 1. If it
is needed later, an Operation Mode can be specified for the Application Program 2 as well. This is
under control by KNX Association.

- In combined devices, the Operation Mode shall be restricted to the executable part that is controlled
by the Application Program Object and not to any other applicative or other layer functionality.

EXAMPLE 8 In a device that would combine an Application Program with the functionality of a (USB) Interface or a Coupler,
that Interface functionality or routing functionality shall not be influenced by the Operation Mode of the Application Program.

© Copyright 1999 - 2021, KNX Association System Specifications v01.10.01 - page 86 of 87

- The MaS does not announce in any way to its communication partners on its current or changed
Operation Mode.

###### 4.4.1.4 Usage by the MaS (device)

- The MaS shall support the Operation Mode as specified in 4.4.1.2.

- The MaS may autonomously reset its Operation Mode back to “Normal Mode”. If the Operation
_Mode times out, then the following shall apply._

   - After each write access to the Operation Mode, the time-out shall at least be 30 s.

   - When the Operation Mode times-out, then the new Operation Mode after this time-out shall be
_Normal Mode._

**Communication Mode and Transport Layer connections**

The MaS shall accept access to Operation Mode both connectionless as well as connection-oriented. The
_Operation Mode shall be independent of the Transport Layer connection and shall not be influenced when_
the Transport Layer connection is opened or closed. Access to the Operation Mode shall not be limited to
the MaC with which there may be an open Transport Layer connection; it may only be limited through
Permissions and Roles.

###### 4.4.1.5 Usage by the MaC

- The MaC shall access the Operation Mode as specified in 4.4.1.2.

- The MaC may at any time read the current Operation Mode and its Time Left using an A_FunctionPropertyState_Read-PDU.

- If the MaS returns a Time Left different from 255 s and the MaC needs the requested Operation
_Mode for a longer time, then the MaC may retrigger the same Operation Mode as many times as_
necessary each time before it expires.

**Communication Modes and Transport Layer connections**

The MaC may address Operation Mode both connectionless as well as connection-oriented.

###### KNX Standard Resources Management

##### 4.5 Router Object (Object Type 6)

###### 4.5.1 General requirements
For the Coupler, all Properties of this Interface Object shall be used both in Line Coupler mode as well as
in Backbone Coupler mode and as well in TP1 Bridge/Repeater Mode.

###### 4.5.2 PID_OBJECT_TYPE (PID = 1)

 4.5.2.1 General requirements
Please refer to clause 4.2.1 for the general requirements of PID_OBJECT_TYPE.

This Property shall contain Object Type of the Interface Object. The Router Object shall have Object
Type 0006h.

###### 4.5.2.2 Usage by the Management Server (device)
PID_OBJECT_TYPE in the Router Object shall support the Data Property services as specified in clause
3.4.3 “Data Property services” of [07] without restrictions.

The Coupler shall additionally support the NM_NetworkParameter_Read_R as follows.

On reception of an A_NetworkParameter_Read-PDU with Object Type = Router Object and
PID = PID_OBJECT_TYPE and test_info = 00h, the Coupler shall respond with an
A_NetworkParameter_Response-PDU with the same service parameter values and with test_result equal
to the Property Value, this is, the Interface Object Type.

This response shall be sent in broadcast communication mode.

The Coupler is in this case addressed itself. Therefore, its handling of the hop_count_type shall be as
specified in [05] clause 2.4.1 “State Machine of Network Layer for normal devices”, this is, when
handling a service indication primitive with hop_count_type equal to 7, respectively different from 7, it
shall in the response primitive use the hop_count_type 7 respectively “Network Layer Parameter”.

- The response shall be transmitted on the Medium Interface on which the request has arrived.

- Additionally, the response may be transmitted also on other Medium Interfaces of the Coupler.

On reception of an A_NetworkParameter_Read-PDU with Object Type = Router Object and
PID = PID_OBJECT_TYPE and test_info ≠ 00h, the Coupler shall not react.

**Error and exception handling**

   - The above applies for any Coupler regardless of the Coupler model (see clause 6.3 in [04]:
KNX Router, KNX TP1 Bridge or KNX TP1 Repeater). The Management Client thus needs to
interpret the Individual Addresses of the responses to conclude on the use of the present
Couplers.

###### 4.5.2.3 Usage by the Management Client
The Management Client may read PID_OBJECT_TYPE with A_NetworkParameter_Read with
hop_count value 0 –to find the nearest Couplers – as well as with value 7.

Please refer to the specification of NM_NetworkParameter_Read in [09] concerning the use of hop_count
value 7.

© Copyright 1999 - 2021, KNX Association System Specifications v01.10.01 - page 90 of 91


-----

 4.5.3 PID_LOAD_STATE_CONTROL (PID = 5)
The Load State Machine in the Router Object shall control the access to the standard Routing Table.

PID_LOAD_STATE_CONTROL in the Router Object shall support the Load Events as listed in
Table 25. For the specification and numerical values of these Load Events, please refer to clause 4.23.2
“Load State Machine – Realisation Type 1 (Property based)”.

based)”.

Unloaded

Loaded

Loading

If the Group Address Routing Table is to be checked on received frames and the Load State is not Loaded
at the same time, no frames shall be routed.

Upon the event Unload the State Machine shall transit to the state Unloaded. It shall not be relied on the
fact that the Routing Table is erased in memory. PID_ROUTETABLE_CONTROL serves to erase the
Routing Table in memory.

The default Load State shall be Loaded and the Routing Table cleared.

/* Announce the status of the medium on one Medium Interface through the remaining Medium Interface. */

It shall be noted that this message does not say what Medium Interface has a problem: the Primary Side or
the Secondary Side. This would even become more imprecise if ever multiple Secondary Sides were reintroduced again. However, even the use of the Object Instances or Object Indexes would not help, as
there are no requirements to these! In broadcast; this message thus only says that one Medium Interface of
this Coupler with IA x.y.z has a problem. (In point-to-point, reading out by the MaC, knowing the
relation between Medium Interface and Object Index or – Type, this does become clear.)

 4.5.7.1 Structure
This Property shall be used for the Management of the Routing Table for standard KNX Group
Addresses. Due to the Property Datatype PDT_Function the configuration is much faster and more
flexible than the standard access to a fixed routing address field. The structure of the Property is defined
in Figure 16.

octet 10 octet 11 octet 12 octet 13 to octet 21

00h or
ServiceID ServiceInfo1 ServiceInfo2 ... ServiceInfo11
return_code

The ServiceID shall specify the selected method. For some methods additional ServiceInfos shall be
necessary.

octet 10 octet 11

00h 01h

The Coupler shall on reception of SRVID_CLEAR_FILTERTABLE clear all standard Group Addresses
in the Routing Table and shall respond with an A_FunctionPropertyState_Response-PDU as follows.

octet 10 octet 11

return_code 01h

 4.5.7.4 ServiceID: 3 (SRVID_CLEAR_GROUPADDRESS)

a) Write (A_FunctionPropertyCommand-PDU)

octet 10 octet 11 octet 12 octet 13 octet 14 octet 15

00h 03h START ADDRESS END ADDRESS

high octet low octet high octet low octet

The Management Client shall apply SRVID_CLEAR_GROUPADDRESS to clear one or more standard
Group Addresses in the Routing Table of the Coupler.

START ADDRESS This shall be the first standard Group Address that shall be cleared.

END ADDRESS This shall be the last standard Group Address that shall be cleared.

If only one standard Group Address is to be modified then START ADDRESS and ENDADDRESS shall
be equal!

If START ADDRESS is greater than END ADDRESS no address will be modified (error response!)

The Coupler shall on reception of SRVID_CLEAR_GROUPADDRESS clear all Standard Group
Addresses in the Routing Table starting from START ADDRESS up to and including END ADDRESS. It
shall respond with an A_FunctionPropertyState_Response-PDU as follows.

Response (A_PropertyPropertyState_Response-PDU)

octet 10 octet 11 octet 12 octet 13 octet 14 octet 15

return_code 03h START ADDRESS END ADDRESS

high octet low octet high octet low octet

The Coupler shall use the following values as return_code.

return_code: 00h: The standard Group Addresses are cleared successfully.

FFh: One or more errors have occurred during the clearing of the standard
Group Addresses (verify error).

###### KNX Standard Resources Management

 4.5.8 PID_COUPL_SERV_CONTROL (PID = 57)
The Property PID_COUPL_SERV_CONTROL in the Router Object (object_type = 6) shall be used to
control SNA management in a Coupler.

**Encoding**

**Bit** **Name** **Description** **(d = default**

**value)**

0 EN_SNA_INCONSISTENCY_CHECK This bit shall enable and disable the inconsistency- 0 = disable (d)
check of frames in point-to-point connectionless 1 = enable
and connection-oriented communication mode.
This feature shall only be executed if the Coupler
is not in TP1 Bridge/Repeater Mode!
See further details below.

1 EN_SNA_HEARTBEAT This bit shall enable and disable “SNA heartbeat” 0 = disable (d)
(see [10] clause 1.3.6 “SNA heartbeat”) in the 1 = enable
Subnetwork connected to the Coupler’s secondary
side.
This feature shall only be executed if the Coupler
is not in TP1 Bridge/Repeater Mode!

2 EN_SNA_UPDATE_WRITE This bit shall enable and disable the update of the 1 = enable
Subnetwork Address by the Coupler in the 0 = disable (d)
Subnetwork Address connected to its secondary
side by an NM_SubnetworkAddress_Write_LocalSubnetwork (see [09]) after its own Individual
Address has changed via programming mode or
KNX Serial Number.
This feature shall only be executed if the Coupler
is not in TP1 Bridge/Repeater Mode!

3 EN_SNA_READ This bit shall enable and disable the server side 0 = disable
support of the SNA read procedure in the Coupler 1 = enable (d)
(see [10]).
If this feature is enabled, the Coupler shall accept
the A_NetworkParameter_Read-service in that
Management Procedure and respond as specified
in [10].
This feature shall only be executed if the Coupler
is not in TP1 Bridge/Repeater Mode! If the Coupler
is in TP1 Bridge/Repeater Mode then this
procedure shall always be ignored, independently
of the Property setting.
See further details below.

4 EN_SUBLINE_STATUS This bit shall enable or disable the distribution of 0 = disable (d)
PID_LINE_STATUS in the Subnetwork connected 1 = enable
to the primary side on power failure and power
return in the Subnetwork Connected to the
secondary side.
This feature shall be executed independent of TP1
Bridge/Repeater Mode!

5 to 7 reserved Shall be 0.

**EN_SNA_INCONSISTENCY_CHECK**
A Router may detect topologically incorrect Individual Addresses on its primary side and on its secondary
side and perform the procedure “SNA update on SNA inconsistency”. The field
EN_SNA_INCONSISTENCY_CHECK shall control whether (enable) or not (disable) the Router shall
detect and correct incorrect Subnetwork Addresses. Please refer to [10] for the specifications.

###### KNX Standard Resources Management

**EN_SNA_READ (indication)**

Newly installed devices may perform an “SNA Read” (see [10]) to get the current SNA. The field
EN_SNA_READ shall control whether (enable) or not (disable) the Router shall react to this procedure or
not. Please refer to [10] for the specifications.

###### 4.5.9 PID_MAX_APDU_LENGTH (PID = 58)

  - Property name: MAX. APDU-Length

  - Property Datatype: PDT_UNSIGNED_INT

  - Datapoint Type: None.

###### 4.5.9.1 Usage by the Management Client
In the Router Object, this Property shall contain the maximal APDU-length of the messages that it can
route from onto the network connection that is controlled through this Router Object instance.

If this Property is not present in the Router Object, the Management Client shall evaluate the same
property PID_MAX_APDU_LENGTH (PID = 56) in the Device Object (see clause 4.3.7).

EXAMPLE If a Management Client needs to find out the maximal APDU-length that it can use to manage (download) a target
device (Management Server) then it also needs to know the maximal APDU-length that is supported by any possible in-between
Router. To this, is shall read PID_MAX_APDU_LENGTH in the Router Object of these Routers. This is specified in [10] under
“Discovery of maximal frame length” Step 3.

###### 4.5.10 PID_L2_COUPLER_TYPE (PID = 59)

  - Property name: L2 Coupler Type

  - Property Datatype: PDT_BITSET8

  - Datapoint Type: None.

###### 4.5.10.1 Format
The Property L2 Coupler Type shall be an 8 bit bitset.

**Bit** **Name** **Value** **Meaning**

0 IS_REPEATER 0 Device is a TP1 Bridge

1 Device is a TP1 Repeater

1 to 7 Reserved 0 These bits are reserved for future extensions.

The default value shall be “TP1 Repeater” (01h).

###### 4.5.10.2 Usage by the Management Server (device)
Bit 0

The Property L2 Coupler Type shall not be evaluated if the device is a Router, this is, if the Device
Address equals 0.

If the Device Address differs from 0 and Property L2 Coupler Type is not implemented, then the Coupler
shall be a TP1 Repeater.

If the Device Address differs from 0 and Property L2 Coupler Type is implemented then the Coupler shall
be a TP1 Bridge if bit 0 equals 0 and a TP1 Repeater is bit 0 equals 1.

© Copyright 1999 - 2021, KNX Association System Specifications v01.10.01 - page 100 of 101

|Bit|Name|Value|Meaning|
|---|---|---|---|
|0|IS_REPEATER|0|Device is a TP1 Bridge|
|0|IS_REPEATER|1|Device is a TP1 Repeater|
|1 to 7|Reserved|0|These bits are reserved for future extensions.|

then Device is Router
else
if PID_L2_COUPLER_TYPE.BIT0 = 0
then Device is TP1 Bridge
else Device is TP1 Repeater
endif
endif

Bit 1 to bit 7

The value of the reserved bits (bit 1 to bit 7) shall be ignored by the Management Server, even if they are
set to 1. In the A_PropertyValue_Response-PDU, confirming the A_PropertyValue_Write-PDU back to
the Management Client, the Management Server (device) shall clear these bits.

###### 4.5.10.3 Usage by the Management Client

4.5.10.3.1 Read access
Bit 0

The Management Client shall interpret this Property Value, in combination with the Device Address of
the Management Server, identically as the Management Server, as specified in 4.5.10.2 above. This shall
allow the Management Client to determine whether the device is a TP1 Repeater or a TP1 Bridge. If this
Property is not present, then the device shall be considered as a TP1 Repeater.

Bit 1 to bit 7

The Management Client shall ignore the value of these bits.

4.5.10.3.2 Write access
**Inputs**

  - Constants

Bit 1 to bit 7: The Management Client shall clear these bits.

  - Application specific

None

  - From user

Bit 0 The value of PID_L2_COUPLER_TYPE.BIT0 shall be provided by the user of
the Management Client.

  - From the Management Server (device)

None.

**Access**

The Management Client shall set the value of Property PID_L2_COUPLER_TYPE using the Procedure
DMP_InterfaceObject_Write_R.

###### KNX Standard Resources Management

 4.5.11 PID_HOP_COUNT (PID = 61)

**●** **Property name:** Hop Count

**●** **Property Datatype:** PDT_UNSIGNED_INT

**●** **Datapoint Type:** None.

**●** **Access levels:** 3/2

**●** **Access Policy:** 3FF/0CC

This Property shall contain the default hop count that the Coupler shall use if it forwards a Frame to the
Medium Interface that is represented by this Router Object.

This Property shall specifically be used if the Frame is forwarded from a KNX Medium that does not
support any hop count, like KNX RF.

If the Coupler acts in the topology as a Line Coupler, the meaningful value for this Property on the
Primary Side is five; if the Coupler in the topology acts as a Backbone Coupler, the meaningful value for
this Property on the Primary Side is four. This way, Frames forwarded by this Coupler on the Primary
Side have the same default hop count as if the Frame would originate from a TP1 Subnetwork.

Please refer to the Profile definitions for the indications for which Primary – or Secondary Sides for
which KNX Communication Media this Property is mandatory.

###### 4.5.12 PID_MEDIUM (PID = 63)

**●** **Property name:** Medium

**●** **Property Datatype:** PDT_ENUM8

**●** **Datapoint Type:** DPT_Medium (20.1004) (see [14])

**●** **Access levels:** 3/X

**●** **Access Policy:** 3FF/0CC

The Property Medium shall indicate the KNX Communication Medium that is used for the Subnetwork
Connected that is represented by this Router Object.

This Property is mandatory for each Router Object, both on the Primary Side as on the Secondary Side.

###### 4.5.13 PID_FILTER_TABLE_USE (PID = 67)

###### 4.5.13.1 Abstract Resource definition
This parameter shall indicate whether the Filter Table shall be used or not.

###### 4.5.13.2 Format and encoding
The parameter Filter Table Use shall be encoded as DPT_Bool (DPT_ID: 1.002).

**Value** **Specification**

0 The Filter Table shall not be used.

1 The Filter Table shall be used.

###### KNX Standard Resources Management

 4.5.13.3 Usage by the Management Server (Coupler)
Please refer to the Abstract Resource definition.

The MaS shall actively interpret this Parameter, even if the implementation specific Coupler Parameters
would allow concluding on whether the Filter Table is used or not.

The MaS shall interpret this parameter Filter Table Use in the routing and filtering functionality as
follows.

**Value** **Interpretation by the MaS**

0 The Filter Table shall not be evaluated.
If the standard - or implementation specific Coupler Parameter values conclude on the
evaluation of Filter Table, then, this evaluation shall return negative for all Group
Addresses.

1 The MaS shall evaluate the Filter Table as specified in 5.3.1.
If the standard - or implementation specific Coupler Parameter values conclude on the
evaluation of Filter Table, then, this evaluation shall be as in 5.3.1.1, and may return
positive or negative accordingly.

This Parameter Filter Table Use may be part of the calculation of the routing condition, as indicated
in [18].

###### 4.5.13.4 Usage by the Management Client
**Writing**

The MaC shall always set this parameter, on any modification of the Filter Table contents or the
(implementation specific) Coupler parameters.

**Value** **Interpretation by the MaC - writing**

0 The FT contents shall be considered as invalid.
The FT shall not be downloaded.

1 The FT contents shall be considered as valid.
The FT shall be downloaded.

**Reading and interpretation**

The MaC shall write this Property parameter during any Configuration (Full download, Partial Download,
Parameters only or any other).

The MaC shall read out this Parameter in status information, device information or in case of reverse
engineering or other.

**Value** **Interpretation by the MaC – reading**

0 The FT contents shall be considered as invalid.
The FT may either be:

− read out but marked invalid, or
− not be read out.

1 The FT contents shall be considered as valid.
The FT may be read out.

 4.5.14 KNX PL110 specific Coupler Properties

 4.5.14.1 PID_PL110_SBC_CONTROL (PID = 104)

**●** **Property name:** PL110 System Broadcast routing control

**●** **Property Datatype:** PDT_FUNCTION

**●** **Datapoint Type:** None

**●** **Access level:** 3/2

**●** **Access Policy:** 3FF/0CC

This Property shall control the Routing of System Broadcast services and shall be evaluated as specified
in [05] clause 2.4.2.4.5.7 “Routing of system broadcast services”. The encoding shall be as follows.

The Functionality of PID_PL110_SBC_CONTROL for PL110 shall be identical to the functionality of
PID_RF_SBC_CONTROL (PID = 112) including the possible deviations through implementation
specific Parameters. Please refer to clause 4.5.15.1 for the specification.

**System broadcast routing Parameters for KNX RF and for KNX PL110**

The parameter for System Broadcast handling for a KNX PL110 connection
PID_PL110_SBC_CONTROL (PID = 104) is not shared with the system broadcast handling parameters
for a KNX RF connection (PID_RF_SBC_CONTROL; PID = 112).

This allows that there may be different parameter sets, - values and – handling between KNX PL110 and
KNX RF.

This could also later on allow for an easy introduction of a PL110/RF Media Coupler.

Mode

The command shall be encoded as specified in Table 27.

- If the MaC sets PID_RF_SBC_CONTROL to “Disable” then the MaS shall immediately deactivate
the routing of system broadcast services. During the first 10 minutes, there shall be no exceptions to
this. After 10 minutes, the value shall remain “Disable” but exceptions through implementation
specific Parameters may apply.

- If the MaC sets PID_RF_SBC_CONTROL to “Broadcast”, then the MaS shall immediately activate
the routing of system broadcast services but shall use broadcast communication mode if routing
these services.

- If the MaC sets PID_RF_SBC_CONTROL to “System Broadcast” then the MaS shall immediately
activate the routing of system broadcast services but shall use system broadcast communication
mode of routing these services.

For both cases “Broadcast” and “System Broadcast”, the MaS shall additionally start a timeout of
10 minutes. If the time-out expires, then the MaS shall autonomously set the value of
PID_RF_SBC_CONTROL to “Disable” again and behave accordingly.

 4.5.16 KNX IP Specific Coupler Parameters

 4.5.16.1 PID_IP_SBC_CONTROL (PID: 120)

**●** **Property name:** IP System Broadcast Routing Control

**●** **Property Datatype:** PDT_FUNCTION

**●** **Datapoint Type:** This Property shall be a Function Property. The coding of the data depends
on whether data is written to the function or responded by the function. No
single DPT can be given.

**●** **Access policy:** 3FF/00C

**●** **Access level:** 2/2

4.5.16.1.1 Abstract Resource definition
This Property shall be used to enable and disable the IP System Broadcast Routing Mode on KNXnet/IP
Routers.

For Coupler 2.0-based implementations, the Properties shall by present in the first (Primary) Router
object.

This Property shall be a Function Property.

Please refer to the above access requirements. These requirements are exclusive: other Roles, security
features or services shall not have access to this Property.

If Security Mode is enabled in the KNXnet/IP Router then this Property shall only be accessible using
Secure Communication. If Security Mode is disabled in the KNXnet/IP Router then this Property shall be
accessible using secure - or plain communication.

The IP System Broadcast Routing Mode shall initially be “Disable”, but can be switched to “Enable” by a
MaC using the Function Property PID_IP_SBC_CONTROL.

The IP System Broadcast Routing Mode shall automatically fall back to “Disable” 20 seconds after it has
been set to “Enable”. It shall be possible for the MaC to prolong the IP System Broadcast Routing Mode
by sending another A_FunctionPropertyCommand-PDU or A_FunctionPropertyExtCommand-PDU with
IP SBC Mode = “Enable” within this timeout. It shall be possible for the MaC to set the IP System
_Broadcast Routing Mode to “Disable” before the timeout elapses by sending another_
A_FunctionPropertyCommand-PDU or A_FunctionPropertyExtCommand-PDU with IP SBC
Mode = “Disable”.

If the MaS provides any facility to block the routing of broadcasts, successfully enabling the IP System
_Broadcast Routing Mode shall also enable the routing of broadcasts. It is implementation-specific if a_
configuration blocking broadcasts prevents enabling the IP System Broadcast Routing Mode with error
code E_COMMAND_IMPOSSIBLE or if the blocking of broadcasts is overruled while the IP System
_Broadcast Routing Mode is enabled._

##### 4.6 LTE Address Routing Table Object (Object Type 7)

###### 4.6.1 General requirements
This Interface Object shall exclusively control the handling of LTE-HEE extended address type frames.

Please refer to [17] for the specification of which Properties are mandatory or optional in the LTE
Address Routing Table Object.

###### 4.6.2 PID_LOAD_STATE_CONTROL (PID = 5)
The Load State Machine in the LTE Address Routing Table Object shall control the access to the LTE
Address Routing Table.

PID_LOAD_STATE_CONTROL in the LTE Address Routing Table Object shall support the Load
Events as listed in Table 31. For the specification and numerical values of these Load Events, please refer
to clause 4.23.2 “Load State Machine – Realisation Type 1 (Property based)”.

**in the LTE Address Routing Table Object**

|Return Code|ErrorName|ErrorType|

these Load Events, please refer to clause 4.23.2 “Load State Machine – Realisation Type 1 (Property
based)”.

**in the LTE Address Routing Table Object**

If the LTE Address Routing Table is to be checked on received frames and the Load State of the LTE
Address Routing Table Object is not Loaded at the same time, no LTE-HEE extended address type
frames shall be routed.

The default Load State shall be Loaded. The LTE Address Routing Table shall be cleared. That means the
current length shall be zero and all LTE-HEE extended address type frames shall be routed.

###### 4.6.4 PID_LTE_ROUTETABLE (PID =52)

  - Property name: LTE Address Routing Table Object

  - Property Datatype: PDT_GENERIC_05

  - Datapoint Type: None

The LTE Address Routing Table shall only be checked if the Property PID_LTE_ROUTESELECT is set
to LTESUB_NORMAL and LTEMAIN_NORMAL. The table shall be a PDT_GENERIC_05 array. The
implementation shall foresee memory space for at least 32 entries. If the current length is zero all for
LTE-HEE extended address type frames shall be routed.

**Attention**

It shall not be forgotten to handle the LTE state machine during the modification of the Routing

###### KNX Standard Resources Management

- Octet 2 und 3: „Base address“

- Octet 4 und 5: „Mask”

**Calculation of the routing condition**

The routing condition shall be calculated as follows.

The LTE Group Address (ZA = Zone Address) in the received Frame shall be compared with the entries
in the LTE Address Routing Table.

routing condition = FALSE;
REPEAT
**IF ((ZA AND Mask) = Base) AND (data direction free) THEN routing condition := TRUE**
/* Note that the EFF is part of LTE Zone Address (Destination Address) and must be included */
/* in the address compare check */
**GOTO next table entry**
**UNTIL (routing condition = TRUE) OR all table entries checked**

**Error – and exception handling**

- MaC
The MaC shall not set reserved values of the EFF-field in this Property.

- MaS
In the Network Layer of the MaS, in the routing of LTE-Frames, there are no requirements
concerning the exception handling of reserved values of the EFF-field.

In the Data Link Layer of the MaS, messages with reserved values of the EFF-field will not be
passed to the Network Layer, even if such entries are contained in the LTE Address Routing Table
_Object of a Coupler or Router, so that the preceding situation will normally not occur._

##### 4.7 cEMI Server Object (Object Type 8)

###### 4.7.1 PID_MEDIUM_TYPE (PID = 51)

  - Property name: Medium Type

  - Property Datatype: PDT_BITSET16

  - Datapoint Type: DPT_Media

This Property shall contain the Media Type(s) supported by cEMI server.

The format complies with the encoding of DPT_Media as specified in [14].

NOTE 23 A cEMI server could be connected to more than one medium[ 9)]; e.g. when the cEMI server device is also a Media
Coupler.

###### 4.7.2 PID_COMM_MODE (PID = 52)

  - Property name: Communication Mode

  - Property Datatype: PDT_ENUM8

  - Datapoint Type: DPT_CommMode (DPT_ID = 20.1000)

Please refer to [12] for the handling and interpretation of PID_COMM_MODE by the cEMI Server.

9) Such a device does not exist yet (May-2002). For separation to which medium a L_Data.req message shall be
sent, respectively from which medium a L_Data.ind message was received, a ‘channel number’ could be defined
as a further ‘additional information’.

###### KNX Standard Resources Management

 4.7.3 PID_MEDIUM_AVAILABILITY (PID = 53)

  - Property name: Medium Availability

  - Property Datatype: PDT_BITSET16

  - Datapoint Type: DPT_Media (DPT_ID = 22.1000)

The Property PID_MEDIUM_AVAILABILITY shall indicate whether the connected medium is active
(availability is true = 1) or not (availability is false = 0).

The same Datapoint Type shall be used as for the Property PID_MEDIUM_TYPE. It shall be a 2 octet
long bit set B16, in which each bit shall indicate if the corresponding medium is active or not. Please also
refer also to 3.2.3.2 “Supported Media Type”.

###### 4.7.4 PID_ADD_INFO_TYPES (PID = 54)

  - Property name: Additional Information Types

  - Property Datatype: PDT_ENUM8[]

  - Datapoint Type: DPT_AddInfoTypes (DPT_ID = 20.1001)

The Property PID_ADD_INFO_TYPES shall indicate which Additional Information Types the cEMI
server supports. If the Property is not present, the cEMI server shall not support any Additional
Information Types.

An array-structured Property shall be used to represent the supported Additional Information Types. Each
(used) array field shall represent one supported Additional Information Type. The Property shall contain
as much array fields as different Additional Information Types are supported. The number of used array
fields (= number of supported Additional Information Types) can be read (read only) as array-element
with start index 0. Within the array, the type IDs shall be sorted in ascending order.

The format of PID_ADD_INFO_TYPES (N8) shall comply with the encoding of DPT_AddInfoTypes as
specified in [14].

The codes DPT_AddInfoType shall be the same as specified in clause “Additional information” in [12].

###### 4.7.5 PID_TIME_BASE (PID = 55)

  - Property name: Time Base

  - Property Datatype: PDT_UNSIGNED_INT

  - Datapoint Type: DPT_Value_2_Ucount (DPT-ID = 7.001)

The Property PID_TIME_BASE shall contain the time base used by the cEMI Server for the extended
relative timestamp. The value shall be the length of one tick of the free running counter used in the
extended relative timestamp in nanoseconds.

Please refer to [12] for the requirements concerning the use of PID_TIME_BASE in the cEMI Server
Object.

 4.7.6 PID_CEMI_SERVER_SNA (PID = 57)

**●** **Property name:** cEMI Server Subnetwork Address

**●** **Property Datatype:** PDT_UNSIGNED_CHAR

**●** **Datapoint Type:** None.

**●** **Access:** - **cEMI Services for local management (M_Prop...)[ 10)]**

**Service:** **M/O**

**Read:** **M**

**Write:** **M**

             - **Data Property services (A_PropertyValue...)[ 11)]**

**Service:** **M/O** **Role:** **Security:** **Access level:**

**Read:** **O** any plain 3

**Write:** **M** MaC plain 2

###### 4.7.6.1 Abstract Resource definition
If there is a cEMI Server Individual Address, then this Property shall contain the Subnetwork Address
part.

###### 4.7.6.2 Format
This field shall be formatted as the Subnetwork Address part of an Individual Address; see clause
“Individual Address” in [04].

###### 4.7.6.3 Usage by the Management Server (device)

4.7.6.3.1 General requirements
This Property shall be the Subnetwork Address part of the Individual Address of the cEMI Server.

- In transmission direction, the cEMI Server shall, unless noted differently in the cEMI message, use
this Individual Address as Source Address.

- In reception direction, unless any other filters are set (e.g. the field “IA” in PID_FILTERING_MODE_SELECT, the cEMI Server shall only forward to the cEMI Client L_Data-messages in pointto-point connectionless – or connection-oriented communication mode that contain this Individual
Address as Destination Address.

The value of this Property shall have immediate effect, this is, it shall be evaluated for the message
received or sent immediately after the setting of this Property.

The Property PID_CEMI_SERVER_SNA shall be stored in non-volatile memory.

4.7.6.3.2 Defending the cEMI Server IA
On USB, the cEMI Client does not explicitly connect to the cEMI Server. The KNX USB interface can
only detect whether the USB cable is connected or not. However, if it is detected that the cable is
connected, then the USB interface shall assume that the cEMI Client is connected.

10) The cEMI services for local device management do not exhibit any security feature. This thus has to be
supported by the cEMI host protocol, like KNXnet/IP Tunnelling or USB.
11) This concerns access via the bus, over the L_Data-service, as well as access through the cEMI Transport Layer
using the cEMI T_Data_Individual or T_Data_Connected to transfer an A_PropertyValue_nnn,-PDU.

###### KNX Standard Resources Management

- If the cEMI Client is **not connected to the cEMI Server, then the cEMI Server shall defend the cEMI**
Server Individual Address: if from the bus a T_Connect-PDU is received addressed to this IA, then
the cEMI Server shall respond with a T_Disconnect-PDU to the sender.

- If the cEMI Client is connected to the cEMI Server then the handling of this T_Connect-PDU shall
depend on the cEMI Communication Mode.

   - If the Communication Mode requires the T_Connect-PDU to be passed to the cEMI Client, then
the cEMI Client shall react to the T_Connect-PDU.

EXAMPLE 3 If the Communication Mode is set to “Data Link Layer” then the T_Connect-PDU shall be passed to
the cEMI Client, who is then responsible to send the T_Disconnect-PDU.

NOTE 24 This could further be blocked by filtering in the Data Link Layer. However, no Data Link
Layer filter settings are defined that allow refusing a point-to-point message to the IA of the cEMI Server. A T_ConnectPDU addressed to the IA of the cEMI Server will thus by the Data Link Layer always be accepted and passed through
Network Layer to the cEMI Client.

   - If the cEMI Communication Mode does not allow or require that that T_Connect-PDU be
passed to the cEMI Client, then the cEMI Server shall react by responding with a T_DisconnectPDU to the sender, which shall contain the cEMI Server IA (PID_CEMI_SERVER_SNA and
PID_CEMI_SERVER_DEVICE_ADDRESS) and not the IA of an end device that may possible
be combined in the USB interface device.

NOTE 25 This is only possible in case the cEMI Communication Mode is set to “cEMI Transport
Layer”. In that case, it is already required i [21] clause 3.5.4.2.2 that “further requests for opening a Transport Layer
connection shall be refused”.

**Accepted exceptions**

3. If the USB cable is connected but no cEMI Client is active and the cEMI Server tries to pass the
T_Connect-PDU to the cEMI Client, then this will not be handled. The IA of the cEMI Server is in
this case not defended.

4. Also, if the cEMI Server operates in Busmonitor Mode, it shall pass the T_Connect-PDU to the
cEMI Client; as however Busmonitor Mode does not allow transmission to the bus, the cEMI Client
cannot send a T_Disconnect-PDU. In this case as well, the cEMI Server IA will not be defended.

5. USB interfaces that are solely powered over USB, and that are for instance not powered over the bus,
can, if the USB cable is disconnected, not defend the IA.

4.7.6.3.3 Accessibility of PID_CEMI_SERVER_SNA
Over the bus, PID_CEMI_SERVER_SNA shall be accessible by Frames addressed to the “mask n IA”. It
shall under no condition – neither in a stand-alone interface nor in combination with a mask n - be
available by Frames addressed to the cEMI Server IA”.

NOTE 26 This is not possible, because the cEMI server IA only allows access to a minimal stack, which does not foresee a
Network Layer or Transport Layer to pass the message to any Management. Frames addressed to the cEMI Server IA will either be
ignored or will be passed to the cEMI Client.

Over the cEMI connection, PID_CEMI_SERVER_SNA shall be accessible using the cEMI services for
local device management (see clause 4.1.7 in [12]).

###### 4.7.6.4 Usage by the Management Client
The Client shall set this Property according the Individual Address that it wants to use for sending and
receiving cEMI L_Data-messages without any further filtering.

It is the responsibility of the cEMI Client to properly set the value of the cEMI Server Individual Address
according the position in the logical topology of the cEMI Server. There are no requirements towards the
cEMI Server to check for correctness or uniqueness of the cEMI Server Individual Address.

NOTE 27 This shall apply for all cEMI Clients: ETS, visualisation tools, etc.

© Copyright 1999 - 2021, KNX Association System Specifications v01.10.01 - page 115 of 116

###### KNX Standard Resources Management

**cEMI Server IA shall differ IA of combined Profile(s)**

If in a single device the KNX RF USB Interface is hosted in combination with one or more other KNX
Profiles, then the MaC shall not use the same value for the IA of any of these implemented Profiles as for
the cEMI Server (PID_CEMI_SERVER_SNA and PID_CEMI_SERVER_DEVICE_ADDRESS in the
cEMI Server Object).

EXAMPLE 10 The KNX RF USB Interface may in one device be combined with an RF end device Profile or with a KNX
TP1/RF Media Coupler. The MaC shall in this case not assign the same numerical IA value to the KNX RF USB Interface
(PID_CEMI_SERVER_SNA and PID_CEMI_SERVER_DEVICE_ADDRESS) as to the end device part, e.g. PID_SUBNET_ADDR
and PID_DEVICE_ADDR in the Device Object.

There are no requirements towards the cEMI Server in this case.

**Defending the cEMI Server IA**

Please refer to 4.7.6.3.2.

###### 4.7.8 PID_BIBAT_NEXTBLOCK (PID = 59)

  - Property name: BiBat Next Block

  - Property Datatype: PDT_UNSIGNED_CHAR

  - Datapoint Type: DPT_Value_1_Ucount (5.010)

This Property is mandatory if the cEMI Server is a BiBat Master.

The cEMI Server that has BiBat Master functionality shall spontaneously send an M_PropInfo.ind
message to the cEMI client with the value of PID_BIBAT_NEXT_BLOCK. It shall contain the number
of the next BiBat block in the Master timeslot scheme. The allowed range is from 0 to 127.

Refer to [12] clause 4.1.5.5.2 “L_Data.req for BiBat synchronous data frames” as well.

###### 4.7.9 PID_RF_MODE_SELECT (PID = 60)

  - Property name: RF Communication Mode

  - Property Datatype: PDT_ENUM8 (alt: PDT_UNSIGNED_CHAR)

  - Datapoint Type: None.

With this Property the RF communication mode of the cEMI Server can be selected.

0: asynchronous (mandatory)

1: asynchronous + BiBat Master (optional)

2: asynchronous + BiBat Slave (optional)

Write access to this Property is optional if only asynchronous RF communication mode is supported.

Layer, thus allowing Local Device Management over the cEMI interface.

0: cEMI Local Transport Layer is not supported.

1: cEMI Local Transport Layer is supported.

The fields b15 to b4 are reserved for future KNX standard extensions and shall be 0.

###### 4.7.13.3 Usage by the Management Server
The cEMI Server shall in this Property indicate the cEMI Communication Modes that it supports, also if
this can be concluded through different means.

EXAMPLE 11 So far (November 2013), each cEMI Server shall support the normal Data Link Layer. Still, this shall be properly
marked here.

EXAMPLE 12 It is required for the mask versions 0310h and 2311h that the Busmonitor Mode is supported. For cEMI on USB,
this can already be concluded reading the Device Descriptor Type 0 using the USB Device Feature services. Yet, this information
shall be repeated here explicitly.

###### 4.7.13.4 Usage by the Management Client
If the cEMI Client does not know the Communication Modes that are supported by the cEMI Server, for
instance because these cannot be concluded based on the DD0, then the cEMI Client shall firstly read this
Property before trying to activate any Communication Mode through PID_COMM_MODE.

###### 4.7.15 PID_FILTERING_MODE_SELECT (PID = 66)

**●** **Property name:** Filtering Mode Selection

**●** **Property Datatype:** PDT_BITSET16 (alt.: PDT_GENERIC_02)

**●** **Datapoint Type:** None

**●** **Access:** - **cEMI Services for local management (M_Prop...)[ 14)]**

**Service:** **M/O**

**Read:** **M**

**Write:** **M**

             - **Data Property services (A_PropertyValue...)[ 15)]**

**Service:** **M/O** **Role:** **Security:** **Access level:**

**Read:** **O** any plain 3

**Write:** **X** none n/a n/a

###### 4.7.15.1 Abstract Resource definition
This Property shall allow the control of the filtering of received Frames by the cEMI Data Link Layer.

###### 4.7.15.2 Format and encoding
**General**

The Data Link Layer of the KNX Communication Media evaluates multiple dependent and subsequent
filters when deciding whether or not to pass a received Frame to the Data Link Layer user or not. With
_Filtering Mode Selection it shall be possible to enable (0) or disable (1) each of these Filters. If a filter is_
disabled, then this shall mean that the evaluation of this Filter shall be seen as positive for the acceptance
of the Frame.

EXAMPLE 13 The Data Link Layer will filter out incoming Frames in point-to-point connectionless or connection-oriented that
have a Destination Address different from the own IA. If this filter is disabled, then the cEMI server will pass all point-to-point
messages to the cEMI Client, regardless of the destination IA (and if the other filter criteria are positive).

© Copyright 1999 - 2021, KNX Association System Specifications v01.10.01 - page 121 of 122

###### KNX Standard Resources Management

Without any filtering switched off, this is, with all fields cleared, the cEMI Data Link Layer shall comply
with the standard KNX Data Link Layer protocol of an end device for the host communication medium.

EXAMPLE 14 It shall only accept Broadcast messages or point-to-point messages if these contain the own Domain Address
(RF medium Object) or respectively the own Individual Address of the cEMI Server. Through this Property, this filtering can be
switched off.

**Default value**

The default value shall be 0, this is, all filters shall be enabled, as for the Data Link Layer of an end
device.

This value shall be assumed
after reset of the cEMI Server, e.g. after restart of the device in which the cEMI Server is hosted,
or on M_Reset.req by the cEMI Client, or
if the cEMI Client sets PID_COMM_MODE to “Data Link Layer”.

The Property PID_FILTERING_MODE_SELECT shall be stored in volatile memory.

**Dependency of filters**

The filters are not independent. An incoming Frame may be accepted by one disabled Filter, but may be
ignored because of another Filter that is still enabled.

EXAMPLE 15 The filter on the Destination IA may be disabled. If an incoming Frame is handled with a DA different than the
own IA, but that it a repeated Frame, then this Frame will still be ignored if not also the filter on repeated Frames is disabled.

**Format**

PID_FILTERING_MODE_SELECT shall be a 2 octet bit field formatted as follows.

**Bit** **Name** **Controlled Filter**

**b0** **IA** **Filter on own IA as Destination Address for Frames in point-to-point**
**connectionless – or connection-oriented communication mode**
0: This filter is not disabled.

Only Frames with the own IA as contained in PID_CEMI_SERVER_SNA
and PID_CEMI_SERVER_DEVICE_ADDRESS in the cEMI Server
Object as Destination Address shall be accepted.
1: This filter is disabled.

These Frames are accepted regardless of the contained DA.
**b1** **Repetitions** **Filter on repeated Frames**
0: This filter is not disabled.

If the interface has successfully received a preceding transmission of
the same Frame, then this repetition shall not be passed to the cEMI
Client.
In KNX RF, this shall mean that the History List shall be evaluated.
This On KNX RF, it means that L2-repetition shall not be accepted.
1: This filter is disabled.

Repeated Frames shall be passed if they meet the further filter criteria.
This field shall signal whether or not repeated Frames shall be passed.
This field shall be evaluated only in an AND-condition with the other fields in
this Property.

EXAMPLE 16 A repeated Frame in ptp communication mode, with a DA different from the
cEMI Server IA, shall only be passed if this bit is set AND if the bit IA is set.

b2 **DoA** **Filter on DoA**
0: This filter is not disabled.

Only Frames with the own DoA as contained in the Device Object shall
be passed to the cEMI Client.
1: This filter is disabled.

All Frames with any DoA shall be passed to the Data Link Layer user.

© Copyright 1999 - 2021, KNX Association System Specifications v01.10.01 - page 122 of 123

###### 4.7.15.3 Usage by the Management Server (cEMI Server)
This is specified in the clause 4.7.15.2 above.

**Default value if the cEMI Client connects to Data Link Layer**

If the cEMI Client sets PID_COMM_MODE of the cEMI Server to Data Link Layer, then the cEMI
Server shall assume the default value (as specified above) for PID_FILTERING_MODE_SELECT.

NOTE 28 As PID_FILTERING_MODE_SELECT only influences the behaviour of the cEMI Server in Data Link Layer mode, this
resetting of the value may be done also when the cEMI Client inactivates Data Link Layer Mode.

The cEMI Server shall also assume the default value for PID_FLTERING_MODE_SELECT if the cEMI
Server is reset in any way.

**Layer-2 acknowledge**

The disabling of a filter shall not influence the Layer-2 acknowledge behaviour of the device in which the
cEMI Server is hosted.

**Error – and exception handling**

1. If a field is set for a filter criterion that is not supported, then the cEMI Server shall behave
according the value zero for that field in the above definition.

###### 4.7.15.4 Usage by the Management Client (cEMI Client)
PID_FILTERING_MODE_SELECT does not foresee mask bits to allow the cEMI Client to selectively
set or clear individual fields without modifying other fields. Therefore, the MaC shall always modify
fields in this Property in a read – modify - write back procedure.

##### 4.8 Group Object Table Object (Object Type 9)

###### 4.8.1 PID_GO_DIAGNOSTICS (PID: 66)

**●** **Property name:** Group Object Diagnostics

**●** **Property Datatype:** PDT_FUNCTION

**●** **Datapoint Type:** None

**●** **Access Policy:** See below.

**●** **Access Level:** 3/3

The Function Property Group Object Diagnostics shall be used by the MaC to set or read the value of a
GO in the MaS and to request the transmission or reading of the GO-value from the bus.

In the commands and responses, the field Group Object Number shall refer to the ASAP, this is, the
Group Object Number in the Group Object Table.

NOTE 29 The Group Object Number is typical S-Mode and is an absolute number of the Group Object for the
entire application. This differs to the Group Object Index, which is typically used in E-Mode and is the number of the
Group Object relative to its E-Mode Channel. See 4.11.16.
The size and contents shall depend on the specific command.

NOTE 30 The functionality of the Property overlaps with the Property PID_OBJECT_VALUE (specified in 4.3.13), used for the
“Group Object Indirection” as required in [08]. That Property however does not support the reading or writing of GO-values from the
bus.

**Access**

The access to PID_GO_DIAGNOSTICS may be implementation specific: it may be accessible in plain
(without KNX Data Security), with authentication or with confidentiality. Additionally, it may be
possible that the access conditions depend on the GO that is being accessed or on the command that is
requested. This can be solved through the implementation of Roles. In any case, Group Object
Diagnostics shall not have lower security access conditions to a GO than the access through the group
services.

EXAMPLE 17 If a GO is only accessible with A+C, then the implementation of GO Diagnostics shall guarantee that
that GO shall also only be accessible at least with A+C.

###### 4.8.1.1 Common requirements

4.8.1.1.1 Interaction of PID_GO_DIAGNOSTICS with the GO-server
PID_GO_DIAGNOSTICS shall access to the Group Objects via the Group Object Server, just like the
standard Group AL-services. Consequently, the commands given through PID_GO_DIAGNOSTICS may
set the communication flags of the Group Object and may be subject to evaluation of the Config flags.

© Copyright 1999 - 2021, KNX Association System Specifications v01.10.01 - page 124 of 125

4.8.1.1.2 Communication flags
The below requirements are specified by - amongst other - referring to the communication flags. The
presence and implementation of these flags is however implementation specific; there are no standard
Resources for these flags. The property PID_GO_DIAGNOSTICS shall not directly access the
communication flags: this shall be done by the standard Group Object Server, as a consequence of the
access by PID_GO_DIAGNOSTICS. In the below commands specification, the indication on the
communication flags is only a possibility and not a requirement.

For the specification of the communication flags, please refer to [08].

4.8.1.1.3 Size of the GO-value
**Alignment**

In the commands and in the responses that carry data, if the data does not fit exactly within the octet
boundary, then it shall be right aligned on the least significant bit positions. Unused bits shall thus be at
the most significant positions. The MaC shall not set unused bits. The MaS shall ignore the value of these
bits.

**Size verification**

The commands foresee a return code for the case when data is written to a GO-value that is too large or
too small.

This is however limited to values written with at least one octet too many or too few.

4.8.1.1.4 Communication Mode and Transport Layer connections
The MaS shall accept access to Group Object Diagnostics both connectionless as well as connectionoriented.

4.8.1.1.5 Operation Mode dependency
The dependency of the Group Object Diagnostics functionality on the Operation Mode is specified for
each command below.

The MaC shall always set the Operation Mode to “Diagnostic Mode” where required. This is indicated in
Table 34 and for each of the below commands. If the MaC changes the Operation Mode, then it shall set
it back to “Normal Mode” when it finishes its GO Diagnostics.

If the MaS does not accept a GO Diagnostics command because of an incorrect Operation Mode, then it
shall respond with the negative Return Code E_COMMAND_IMPOSSIBLE (see below).

(Write – or read-request).
03h Transmit request There is a transmission requested for this GO-value

(Write – or read-request) but it has not yet started.

The Transmission Status “Transmitting” and “Transmit request” are intermediate states. It is not
required that the MaS supports these states. If the MaS returns any of these states, then the MaC
shall leave the MaS and the KNX network sufficient time to complete request, typically 6 s and
read the final result by a subsequent “ReadServiceID 01h – Get local GO value” (see 4.8.1.4.3),
until either “”Idle; OK” or “Idle; Error” is returned.

The encoding of these fields Update and Data Request shall be identical as in the
Communication Flags in the RAM-Flags-Table in (4.18.3.1.1.1).

###### KNX Standard Resources Management

4.8.1.3.2 WriteServiceID 00h - Set local GO value
The MaC shall use this command to set the value of a GO in the MaS. This shall allow the MaC to check
whether an unexpected behaviour of the MaS may be due to an ignoring of the message by the MaS due
to KNX Data Security restrictions (e.g. Roles and Permissions) or due to another reason, e.g. at
application level or in the communication stack.

**Operation Mode dependency**

The MaS shall make the command “Set local GO value” available exclusively in the following Operation
Modes.

   - Normal Mode

   - Diagnostic Mode

An overview of the Operation Mode dependency of the commands is given in Table 34.

**Command execution**

The Group Object Server in the MaS shall accept the command. This command shall not be subject to
further checking of Permissions and Roles. This command shall be handled as an accepted
A_GroupValue_Write-PDU for the GO. Its result shall however still be subject to the Group Object
Config Flags for the GO. If the GO-value can be written, then the GO Server may set the update-flag of
the GO. The execution of this command does not require that the MaS sends the value of this GO on the
bus. However, it may be that the subsequent normal behaviour of the application causes a transmission of
the GO-value, e.g. if there is a COV-condition for the transmission. In the same way, the command
execution does not require that other GOs in the MaS that may be linked to the same GAs as this GO shall
be influenced, but this may be a consequence of the application.

NOTE 35 This is thus to be interpreted as if an A_GroupValue_Write-PDU is received from the bus for this GO. It relates in the
same way to the Config flags and the communication flags. It differentiates from receiving a Frame from the bus, as it for instance
will not use GAs in the GA-Table or links in the Association Table.

NOTE 36 This command operates at the level of the Group Object and not at the level of the Group Address. Other Group Objects
in the MaS that are linked to the same GA(s) as the GO that is accessed will not change value. To test for instance a “central off”
functionality one would rather trigger the transmission at a sending GO using “WriteServiceID 01h - ” or “WriteServiceID 02h - Send
local GO value on bus”.

###### KNX Standard Resources Management

- Flags: **Bit** **7** **6** **5** **4** **3** **2** **1** **0**
**Field**

S r r r r r

0 0 0 0 0

                  - Bit 7 (msb) “Selector” (S)
This flag shall indicate whether the Data shall be sent if possible in
the 6 trailing bits after the 4 bit APCI in the field “data/APCI” in the
A_GroupValue_Write-PDU.
This flag shall only be evaluated in case the field Data has a length
of 1 octet and a value of less than 64.

0: The data shall be included in the 6 trailing bits “data/APCI”
after the 4 bit APCI.
1: The data shall be included in the first next full octet after
the 4 bit APCI.

In case the field Data is 1 octet long and has a value equal to or
larger than 64 or in case the length is longer than 1 octet (even if the
value is smaller than 64), the MaS shall ignore the value of this flag.
This shall not be a condition for reporting with an error or for
refusing the command.

                  - Bits 6 to 2 are reserved for further standard extensions and shall be
0.

                  - Bits 1 and 0 (lsb) shall have the same meaning as the GO Security
flags as specified in [07].

- Group Address: This shall be the target GA of the Telegram to be sent.

- Data: This shall be the value that shall be sent on the bus.

The MaS shall do the following actions.

1. The MaS shall initiate the transmission of an A_GroupValue_Write-Telegram on the bus on the
requested GA and according the requested Flags.

If the Flags require the use of Data Security, then the MaS shall accordingly secure the
outgoing message using its own Sequence Number Sending and the key as found for the
requested GA in its Group Key Table. Errors resulting from this shall be responded to the
MaC with the appropriate Return Code.

The Return Code shall however be independent of the success or failure of the actual
transmission. Failure of transmission, absence of a Layer 2 acknowledge for media where
this is supported or Layer 2 repetitions shall for this not lead to a negative Return Code.

2. The MaS shall additionally pass an A_GroupValue_Write.ind to its own Application Layer with
the used security service parameters (par_auth and par_conf) from the command; the link_index
shall be “None”. All GOs linked to the requested GA shall be updated if this is accepted
according these flags and according their GO config flags.

The MaS shall not inform the MaC on the outcome of this action, regardless of whether
none, only a subset or all of the linked GOs is updated. (Please refer to the indications
concerning reading out the local GO-values and the possible retries in [09] clause
DMP_GA_DIAGNOSTICS_RCl).

The MaS shall handle this command 01h just as command 00h and initiate the update of
the GO-value, ignoring possible Roles and Permissions. However, the GO Config flags
shall be evaluated for setting the local GO-value.

NOTE 38 This means that the W-flag shall be evaluated for the setting of the GO-value through this command.
