 6.3.15.2 Security
Please refer to the above access requirements. These requirements are exclusive: other Roles, security
features or services shall not have access to this Property.

Please refer to clause 1.3 as well.

**Format**

The Group Object Security Flags shall be an array Property of which each element shall contain the
Security Config Flags for one Group Object in the Group Object Table with the same index.

The Security Config Flags of one entry, for one Group Object, shall be formatted as defined in Figure 81.

b7 b6 b5 b4 b3 b2 b1 b0

**Figure 81 – Group Object Security Flags**

Each entry shall be an 8 bit value. Only the bits b1 and b0 are defined. The bits b7 to b3 are reserved for
future extensions and the MaC shall always write these bit values with 0. The MaS shall ignore these
reserved bits.

###### 6.3.15.3 Usage by the MaS (device)
The MaS shall evaluate the Group Object Security Flags as part of the handling of the incoming service
primitives of A_GroupValue_Read and A_GroupValue_Write, this is, in the AIL. These will only be
verified if these messages are accepted and passed by the S-AL. This is, these flags will not be evaluated
if there are errors in the SeqNr or the security (MAC verification, decryption).

Bits b1b0 shall specify the KNX Security features for the Group Object[ 99)]. These flags shall be used for
all service primitives of the A_GroupValue_Read– and the A_GroupValue_Write-service.

### Use cases for Group Object Diagnostics

##### A.1 Use case 1: set the value of a GO to diagnose its proper working
**Description**

The User experiences that a Group Object is not reacting to messages from the bus. KNX Data Security is
used and the user wants to exclude that the communication or functional problem is due to KNX Data
Security.

The User uses Group Object Diagnostics to set the Group Object in point-to-point communication. If the
Group Object with this behaves as expected, the User may narrow down the malfunction to KNX Data
Security (wrong keys, Sequence Numbers not synchronised, wrong senders IAs in receiver…). If the
Group Object still behaves wrongly, then the cause may rather be searched in the configuration of the
device (parameters or other).

##### A.3 Use case 3: path check
**Description**

The user experiences that the SwitchingActuator (1.1.2) appears not to react to the Telegrams of a
BinaryInput (1.1.1). It is suspected that the Telegrams from the BinaryInput are not received by the
SwitchingActuator. For this, the BinaryInput is forced to send a Telegram and it is checked if the
SwitchingActuator effectively receives that Telegram.

The MaC limits the group communication of the SwitchingActuator to the Individual Address of the
BinaryInput (1.1.1) and then forces the BinaryInput to send a group message (to the SwitchingActuator)
with a certain value NewValue. If the MaC now reads the state and value of this GO in the
SwitchingActuator and finds that the Update-flag is set and the new value is accepted, then the user may
conclude that the communication between both devices is working well.

© Copyright 1999 - 2021, KNX Association System Specifications v01.10.01 - page 352 of 353


-----

###### KNX Standard Resources Management

- The MaC shall firstly read the status and value of the GO through a first command
GetLocalGOValue.

   - If the returned current GO-value “value” equals the value “NewValue” that the MaC intends to
set next, then the MaC user should be warned that the reception of NewValue can possibly not
unambiguously be detected.

   - If the returned E_GD_GO_STATUS_VALUE signals that the Update-flag is currently set, then
the MaC shall repeat the request every 1 s until it receives a response in which this flag is
cleared or until 6 s in total have passed. If after that the Update-flag is still set, the MaC shall
signal to the MaC user that the application does not seem to properly handle a preceding
message from the bus.

- To prevent that the SwitchingActuator clears the Update-flag before it can be read by the MaC and
possibly changes the GO-value, the MaC will firstly set the Operation Mode to “Diagnostic Mode”
in the SwitchingActuator.

- In order to avoid that in the SwitchingActuator in-between the GroupValueWrite(NewValue) from
the BinaryInput and the GetLocalValue() from the MaC the value of the GO changes by a
coincidental transmission by e.g. a Switch (1.1.3), the MaC will firstly limit the group
communication in the SwitchingActuator to the IA (1.1.1) of the BinaryInput.

###### KNX Standard Resources Management

##### A.5 Use case 5: write group message from ETS
**Description**

The MaC (ETS) offers the functionality to send group messages (A_GroupValue_Read and
A_GroupValue_Write) from the Group Monitor or from the GA-view. This will for secure GAs however
not work as for plain GAs.

   - The MaC (ETS) cannot send an S-A_Data-PDU encrypted with the Tool Key using that GA.

According KNX Data Security receivers shall refuse an S-A_Data-PDU received with a
T_Data_Group.ind if it is protected with the Tool Key.

Additionally the MaC (ETS) assigns a different, unique Tool Key to each different MaS
(device), only the MaS of which the Tool Key is used would properly receive the secure
message and handle the message it; the other participants in the group will not handle the
message.

   - The MaC (ETS) could send an S-A_Data-PDU encrypted with the Group Key used by all MaS
for that GA.

This requires that the MaC (ETS) to this purpose uses an IA that is present in the Security
Individual Address Table. This is not the case.

As solution, the MaC (ETS) selects one MaS (device) that is capable of sending on this GA and make this
MaS (device) send the message on behalf of the MaC (ETS).

**Sequence**

1. From all devices that are associated with this GA, the MaC (ETS) selects one as its MaS.

If such GO cannot be found, the MaC user shall be informed.

2. The MaC (ETS) executes the command WriteServiceID 01h - Send A_GroupValue_Write on
the chosen MaS.

3. The MaS (device) confirms with the Return Code E_SUCCESS (00h).

4. The MaS sends an A_GroupValueRead_Write-PDU on the bus.

##### A.6 Use case 6: read group message from ETS
**Description**

Please refer to the introduction of “Use case 5: write group message from ETS” above for the problem
description.

In this use case, the MaC (ETS) user wants to “read the value of a GA” from the bus. Also in this
solution, the MaC (ETS) choses a helper device that will perform the A_GroupValue_Read.

**Constraints (informative)**

- In case of an A_GroupValue_Read, the MaC will only be able to receive the response if it is located
in the same Subnetwork as the responding device or if the Coupler Filter Tables between the MaC
and the responding device are open for this Group Address. This is the same situation as today.
This restriction could be bypassed if the MaC is notified by the MaS about any responses. For now,
this is out of scope.

**Sequence**

1. From all devices that are associated with this GA, the MaC (ETS) selects one as its MaS.
If such GO cannot be found, the MaC user shall be informed.

2. The MaC (ETS) executes the command WriteServiceID 03h – Send A_GroupValue_Read on
the chosen MaS.

3. The MaS (device) confirms with the Return Code E_SUCCESS (00h).

4. The MaS sends an A_GroupValueRead_Read-PDU on the bus.

5. If the MaC is interested in the further result of this command then it will perform the following
loop, while the GO Status is “Transmit Request” or “Transmitting” and the 6 s timeout has not
elapsed.

    - The MaC executes the command ReadServiceID 01h - Get local GO value on the MaS.

    - The MaS shall confirm with the Return Code E_GD_GO_STATUS_VALUE, which
contains the current GO Status.

    - Meanwhile, any other device may respond on the bus with an
A_GroupValue_Response-PDU containing a Value.

The MaS may read the result of the operation either from the updated value of the used GO in
the helper device, as contained in the E_GD_GO_STATUS_VALUE, or it may receive and use
the A_GroupValue_Response-PDU send by any other device directly from the bus.

NOTE 114 This has the side effect that the GO value of the MaS will be changed if the U flag is set. This is
considered acceptable as it is normal runtime behaviour that also occurs today if the MaC (ETS) sends a
A_GroupValue_Read-PDU.

###### KNX Standard Resources Management

### Annex B
###### (informative)

#### Examples of table implementations

##### B.1 Introduction
This annex gives informative examples of how the Resources may be implemented on KNX RF. For
KNX RF, these Resources are not standardised and not mandatory. The configuration of KNX RF devices
uses dedicated services in function of the Configuration Mode, as specified in [10]. Also the S-Mode
access to KNX RF devices is specified without requiring certain formats of the Resources.

##### B.2 Extension of KNX to enable use of Extended Addresses

###### B.2.1 Existing resources from KNX B.2.1.1 Object table (Datapoint Table)
The list of Datapoints used by a device is defined in the Datapoint Table.

Datapoint# Datapoint Table
Length (1octet)
0 Datapoint description #0 (3 octets)
1 Datapoint Description #1 (3 octets)
2 Datapoint description #2 (3 octets)
3 ….. …..

Each Datapoint is identified by an index called Datapoint#.

Property access:

Group object table Interface Object / PID_TABLE = 23 Group Object Table

###### B.2.1.2 Address Table
Address# Address Table
Length (1octet)
0 Individual Address (2 octets)
1 Group Address = @bank + @link (2 octets)
2 Group Address = @bank + @link (2 octets)
3 ….. …..

Each address is identified by an index called address# . There is no need to make the separation into
@bank and @link.

Property access:

Address Table Interface Object / PID_TABLE = 23 Address table Property format 0

###### B.2.2 New resources
The list of Extended Group Address used in a device is defined by two tables:

- Serial number table, and

- an Association Table to link Group Addresses and Serial Number to build Extended Addresses.

###### B.2.2.2 New Association Table
To enable that a Datapoint can be part of multiple groups (e.g. multiple push-buttons command one lamp,
one for on/off and a second for general off), an Association Table is used. This assocition links one
Datapoint with one or more Extended Group Address (couple of Address and Serial Number).

Each association is defined by

- Address index (1octet),

- Serial Number index (1 octet),

- Datapoint index (1 octet).

Association table
Length (1octet)
Address # Serial # Datapoint# (3 octets)

If a Datapoint is transmit only, the association Serial Number index equals FFh. No Serial Number can be
associated.

**Rules**

The association of the sending Datapoint must be at the beginning of the Association Table.

**The Serial Number Table Interface Object**

The Serial Number Table Object includes Serial Numbers of devices linked to the device. It provides the
management operations for downloading.

###### B.3.1 Existing object
The Association Table Object is used to connect Group Objects to Group Addresses. It provides the
management operations for downloading.

The Association Table Property contains associations between the communication number and the
Service Access Point (SAP). The maximum number of elements in the Property shows the maximum size
of the table and current length shows the current usage. In each association the high octet is the
communication number and the low octet is the SAP number.

In case of sending the first entry in the Association Table shall be used.

If the current length is set to 0 a standard a Association Table shall be used
(communication number + 1 = SAP number). The Maximum Length shall be transferred with the load
control MAX_LENGTH or shall be fixed in the device.

###### B.3.2 New Property : Association Table format 1
To enable use of Extended Group Addresses, the association must be made between a Serial Number, a
Group Address and a Group Object. For this a new format is designed for the Association Table Object.

The existing one just changes its Property name from Association_Table to Association_Table_format0.
The new one gets the Property name Associtaion_Table_Format1.

**Table 112 - Association table Interface Object**

In the Association table format 1, one entry consist of an association of a Serial Number index, a
communication number and the Service Access Point (SAP). The maximum number of elements in the
Property shows the maximum size of the table and current length shows the current usage. In each
association, the octet 2 is Group Address index, the octet 1 is the Serial Number index and the octet 0 is
the Group Object index.

In case of sending the first entry in the association table is used.

For Association for extended Individual Addresses have the datapoint index equal to FFh.

###### B.4.2 Use of tables for sending
In case of sending the Serial Number used is always the one of the product, and not the one from the
Extended Address associated to the Datapoint. The column of serial index (serial#) is not used in sending.
The Serial Number of the product is stored in an other place of the memory (it is not easy to implement a
length variable table with a Serial Number factory written). The first association found in the table is used
for the transmission.
